name: introduction-bullets
text: Discarded cigarettes and delayed smoke can precede serious fires. AI Fireguard uses YOLOv5 to localise cigarette, flame and smoke for earlier human-verified alerts and later response planning.

name: evidence-boundary-band
text:
ERRORS, LIMITATIONS & NEXT STEPS
• Cigarette recall 0.634: small targets and hand occlusion remain difficult.
• Flame recall 0.740, but AP@0.5:0.95 0.360: localisation needs improvement.
• Smoke leads in precision (0.919) and strict AP (0.595), but recall is 0.667.
• One-image inference and batch timing are not deployment evidence.

NEXT
Add low-light, occlusion, fog and steam hard negatives; calibrate each class; test temporal consistency and unseen buildings; connect only verified alerts to the escape-route prototype.

name: section-V-Conclusion
text: V. Conclusion
textPreview: V. Conclusion

name: conclusion-bullets
text:
• Leakage auditing changed the scientific conclusion: the legacy checkpoint fell from an apparent validation mAP@0.5 of 0.889 to 0.084 on the clean test.
• Retraining recovered mAP@0.5 to 0.755 and mAP@0.5:0.95 to 0.453 on a genuinely independent split.
• This equals 85% of the legacy artifact's headline AP50 while providing credible generalisation evidence.
• The detector is promising for human-verified alerts, but missed small/occluded targets and localisation error preclude safety-critical deployment.
